description.value: The study tested whether medial orbitofrontal cortex gray matter volume is reduced in abstinent substance-dependent individuals relative to control subjects and whether medial OFC gray matter relates to decision-making performance and substance-dependence symptoms.

design.value: A cross-sectional between-group voxel-based morphometry study comparing 19 abstinent substance-dependent individuals with 20 control subjects, with whole-brain and medial OFC region-of-interest analyses and partial correlations with modified gambling-task performance and CIDI-SAM symptom counts.

name.value: International Consortium for Brain Mapping (ICBM) tissue probability maps
computerized Composite International Diagnostic Interview Substance Abuse Module (CIDI-SAM)

description.value: A structured interview for measuring drug dependence; for each drug, symptom count and date of last use were recorded.

A modification of the IGT adapted for a functional magnetic resonance imaging experiment, consisting of 80 trials in which subjects chose “Play or Pass”; choices to play “bad” decks were totaled for early and late trial blocks.

name.value: two-subtest Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence

description.value: Vocabulary and Matrix Reasoning subtests were administered to measure IQ.

source_definition.value: IQ measured on the basis of the two-subtest Wechsler Abbreviated Scale of Intelligence
repeated measures analysis of variance analyzing for effects of group × time interaction
2 × 2 (gender, group) ANOVA evaluating gender × group interactions

name.value: number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks

source_definition.value: The number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks on early compared with late trials was totaled.
GM volume obtained from the voxel corresponding to the global maxima of the group difference model that localized to medial OFC (−5, 53, −5, Montreal Neurological Institute)
The hypothesis was that a higher GM would correlate with greater avoidance of “bad” cards.

association_direction.value: negative correlation with medial OFC GM volume

task_description.value: A modification of the IGT adapted for a functional magnetic resonance imaging experiment that simulates uncertainty and reward of real-life decision-making.

design_type.value: repeated-measures design with early and late trial blocks

stimuli.value: Gambling decks, including “bad” decks, with uncertainty and reward consequences.

task_performance_measures.value: number of times an individual chose to play “bad” decks on early compared with late trials

instrument.value: 3-T whole body MR scanner (General Electric, Milwaukee, Wisconsin) with a standard quadrature head coil

description.value: A high-resolution three-dimensional T1-weighted spoiled gradient echo (SPGR)-IR sequence was acquired in the coronal plane. Scan time was 9 min 24 sec.

instrument.value: 3-T whole body MR scanner (General Electric, Milwaukee, Wisconsin) with a standard quadrature head coil

description.value: The echo planar T2* images were evaluated for gross structural abnormalities, particularly encephalomalacia.

Voxel-based morphometry processing combined tissue segmentation, bias correction, and spatial normalization into a unified model. Hidden Markov Random Fields were applied to improve tissue-segmentation accuracy, brains were normalized to ICBM tissue probability maps, and images were smoothed with a 12-mm full-width-at-half-maximal Gaussian kernel, resulting in final smoothing of 14 × 15 × 14 mm³.

steps.value: spatial normalization into a unified model
Hidden Markov Random Fields with medium HMRF .3
normalization to tissue probability maps provided by International Consortium for Brain Mapping (ICBM)

model_settings.value: At the second level, whole brain data were modeled across the groups with total GM volume and age as covariates. Statistical maps were set at a cluster-level threshold of p < .05, corrected for multiple comparisons with family-wise error (FWE), and a voxel-level threshold of p < .005.

software.value: VBM5.1 implemented in SPM5 running on Matlab 7.5

model_settings.value: A region-of-interest analysis of right and left medial OFC was implemented with the Automated anatomic labeling (AAL) ROI library within Marsbar SPM toolbox.
Repeated measures ANOVA with IQ, education, and age as covariates, analyzing effects of group × time interaction.
Partial correlation between GM volume and behavioral data adjusted for IQ, education, and total GM; considered significant at p < .05, one-tailed.
Partial correlation between symptom count and medial OFC GM volume, adjusted for total GM, IQ, and age.

A 2 × 2 (gender, group) ANOVA with covariates of age and total GM and multiple comparison correction, evaluating main effects of gender and gender × group interactions on GM volume and decision-making behavior.
The authors subsequently analyzed whether OFC GM correlated with abstinence; no relationship between abstinence and morphology was found.

definition.value: Control subjects > SDI; ANCOVA covarying for global GM and age

interpretations.value: Reduced medial OFC GM might reflect long-term adaptations within the reward-learning circuit underlying pathological decision-making in substance dependence.
